question: Which statement best describes Page title?
options: A page title names a page in browser tabs, bookmarks, and search results. Make it specific and put the main subject early. It is like labeling each folder so people can tell them apart. Repeating the same title across a site makes pages harder to distinguish. For example, a unique title helps distinguish two articles about similar subjects. In a real page, write a title that distinguishes a product detail page from the product category.

Structured data gives machines a standard description of a page entity, such as an article or product. JSON-LD is a common format. It is like adding a catalog card with labeled fields. The data must match visible content and does not guarantee enhanced search results. For example, a product JSON-LD block should match its visible name and price. In a real page, ensure a JSON-LD price matches the price shown to visitors.

Crawlers discover pages through links and sitemaps. Important routes need stable addresses and links that can be followed. It is like creating connected paths through a library. Client navigation should still deliver useful page content and direct URLs should work. For example, a sitemap can help crawlers discover stable routes but does not guarantee indexing. In a real page, link important routes from ordinary navigable pages so crawlers can discover them.

A description summarizes what a page offers, while headings create a readable outline. These details should match what visitors can actually find. It is like writing an accurate catalog entry and chapter labels. Search engines may choose other text for a preview, so do not promise a guaranteed snippet. For example, a heading outline should describe sections that are visibly present on the page. In a real page, use headings that describe visible article sections in order.

Repeating the same title across a site makes pages harder to distinguish. For example, a unique title helps distinguish two articles about similar subjects. In a real page, write a title that distinguishes a product detail page from the product category.

question: Which statement best describes Description and headings?
options: Robots directives can ask search engines not to index a page. Use them carefully for duplicate or temporary content. They are not access controls. It is like putting a “do not list” note on a public door; private content still needs server-side authorization. For example, use authorization rather than robots metadata to protect private account content. In a real page, protect private dashboards with authentication even when they are marked noindex.
